newsitem.title: USA: Freeze likely in northern U.S. Midwest Friday.
newsitem.headline: Freeze likely in northern U.S. Midwest Friday.

text.p: Below freezing temperatures were forecast for the northern U.S. Midwest Friday morning with the frost line extending from Peoria, Ill., to Dayton, Ohio, meteorologists said.
"It looks like we're going to have freezing temperatures in areas we haven't seen them yet," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Lows were expected to range from 30 to 32 degrees Farenheit with some 20s possible in the north, he said.
But warmer weekend temperatures were expected to follow the brief cold snap.
"It will be a very chilly morning tomorrow and then we're going to start to bring the warming temperatures in for the weekend," Palmerino said.
Weekend highs could reach the 70s F in some areas but little rainfall was expected with the warmer temperatures, said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis.
"It's going to be tough during the next week or so for any spot in the corn belt to see .25 inch in a 24-hour period," he said. "Most days seem to be on the dry side with quite a bit of sunshine."
Long-range forecasting models indicated a slight cool-down early next week but the projections moderated from Wednesday's outlook for very cold temperatures, meteorologists agreed.

"Today's maps have backed off considerably on that," Solberg said, referring to the cold temperatures. "It looks like a brief shot of below normal temperatures but nothing that much out of the ordinary for this time of year."
Palmerino said the weather pattern later next week should bring normal to above normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation.
